Tuesday, April 22, 2025  7:00 PM  Council Chamber

NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's web site under City Council Meeting agendas at www.RollingHillsEstates.gov and
  during regular business hours in the office of the City Clerk. Meetings are live broadcast on the City's web
  site and a recording is available for viewing after each meeting. Meetings are also broadcast on PVP -TV
  Channel 35 (Cox) and Channel 39 (Verizon).

  Public Comment is welcome on any item during City Council consideration of the item. An opportunity is
  also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. If you would like to
  address the City Council regarding an item on this agenda or make a general public comment, please
  complete a speaker sheet and give to the City Clerk.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  APRIL 22, 2025

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR STEGURA called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by the members of the Palos Verdes Symphonic Band.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Development Director Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Assistant to the City Manager Jessica Slawson
  Senior Accountant Fernando Estrada

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION DECLARING APRIL 24, 2025 AS A "DAY OF REMEMBRANCE" OF
  THE ARMENIAN GENOCIDE OF 1915-1923

MAYOR STEGURA presented a proclamation declaring April 24, 2025 as a day of
remembrance of the Armenian Genocide of 1915-1923, and MAYOR PRO TEM
ZERUNYAN provided a brief history of the Armenian Genocide.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN exited the Council Chambers at 7:30 p.m.

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-G AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

B.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  APPROVED.

C.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF APRIL 2025

  APPROVED WARRANTS 68407 THROUGH 68461 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $188,211.12 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 040125 THROUGH
  040325 IN THE AMOUNT OF $136,080.60 FOR A GRAND TOTAL AMOUNT
  OF $324,002.20 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

D.  SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS REPORT OF MARCH 2025

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
APRIL 22, 2025
 E.  REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT OF MARCH 2025

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF APRIL 8, 2025

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

G.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF MARCH 24, 2025

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT/PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

None.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

None.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  ANNUAL AUDIT ENGAGEMENT LETTER TASK ORDER 2025-01

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve Task Order No. 2025-01 for the firm
  of Rogers, Anderson, Malody & Scott, LLP to perform the annual audit and report for
  Fiscal Year 2024-25; perform the single audit, if needed; prepare the Pepper Tree
  Foundation’s tax returns; and review the GANN appropriation limitation for a total
  amount not to exceed $51,405.

Senior Accountant Estrada provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

MAYOR STEGURA confirmed that there was a typo in the staff report and the amount listed
in the Task Order was the accurate amount.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHACHTER, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  APPROVE TASK ORDER NO. 2025-01 FOR THE FIRM OF ROGERS,
  ANDERSON, MALODY & SCOTT, LLP TO PERFORM THE ANNUAL AUDIT
  AND REPORT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2024-25; PERFORM THE SINGLE AUDIT,
  IF NEEDED; PREPARE THE PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION’S TAX
  RETURNS; AND REVIEW THE GANN APPROPRIATION LIMITATION FOR A
  TOTAL AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $51,405.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura
  ABSENT:  Zerunyan

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN returned to the Council Chambers at 7:36 p.m.

B.  AUTHORIZATION TO APPROVE A TEMPORARY ACCESS EASEMENT BETWEEN
  THE CITY AND COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES FOR TRAIL ACCESS ON THE PALOS
  VERDES LANDFILL FOR THE PURPOSE OF HAYRIDES OPERATED BY PETER
  WEBER EQUESTRIAN CENTER

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Temporary Access Easement
  Agreement between the City and the County of Los Angeles for trail access to provide
  hayrides at the Peter Weber Equestrian Center.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
APRIL 22, 2025
 Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ highlighted the Equestrian Committee’s discussion on this
item, and emphasized that it is a very specific area and specific timing for the use of this area
for hayrides.

Assistant City Manager Davis explained there were some challenges that the Sanitation
Districts staff was experiencing with public use at the PV Landfill site, and activities were
paused for some time during 2023, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER suggested informing the Palos Verdes Peninsula
Horseman’s Association, in addition to the boarders.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE THE TEMPORARY ACCESS EASEMENT AGREEMENT
  BETWEEN THE CITY AND THE COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES FOR TRAIL
  ACCESS TO PROVIDE HAYRIDES AT THE PETER WEBER EQUESTRIAN
  CENTER.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

9.  OLD BUSINESS

None.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ attended the California Contract Cities Association’s (CCCA)
April Board meeting where the outgoing CCCA President, Jennifer Perez, was honored.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF attended the South Bay Cities Council of Governments (SBCCOG)
Transportation Committee meeting and will be attending the Cal Cities City Leaders Summit
this week.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN will be attending the SCAG General Assembly May 1 – 2.

MAYOR STEGURA attended the Clean Power Alliance (CPA) April Board Meeting, the April
Peninsula Mayor’s Lunch, the Los Angeles County Sanitation Districts April Board meeting,
and today was a panelist at the Palos Verdes Peninsula Association of Realtors® (PVPAR)
Peninsula Mayor’s Breakfast. Lastly, this week she plans to attend the SBCCOG Board
meeting.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

A.  LETTER OF SUPPORT TO ASSEMBLY BILL 650 (PAPAN): PLANNING AND
  ZONING: HOUSING ELEMENT: REGIONAL HOUSING NEEDS ALLOCATION

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the Mayor to sign a letter in support
  of AB 650 (Papan): Planning and Zoning: Housing Element: Regional Housing Needs
  Allocation.

Assistant to the City Manager Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
APRIL 22, 2025
 Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AUTHORIZE THE MAYOR TO SIGN A LETTER IN SUPPORT OF AB 650
  (PAPAN): PLANNING AND ZONING: HOUSING ELEMENT: REGIONAL
  HOUSING NEEDS ALLOCATION.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

B.  LETTER OF OPPOSITION TO ASSEMBLY BILL 647 (GONZALEZ): HOUSING
  DEVELOPMENT APPROVALS: RESIDENTIAL UNITS

  Recommendation: That the City Council authorize the Mayor to sign the letter of
  opposition to AB 647 (Gonzalez): Housing development approvals: residential units.

Assistant to the City Manager Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Assistant to the City Manager Slawson explained that criterion for allowing exclusions is written
within the legislative text, and the zones are defined by each respective regulating agency of
that designation, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AUTHORIZE THE MAYOR TO SIGN THE LETTER OF OPPOSITION TO AB
  647 (GONZALEZ): HOUSING DEVELOPMENT APPROVALS: RESIDENTIAL
  UNITS.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

13.  CLOSED SESSION

None.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 7:53 p.m. MAYOR STEGURA adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, May 13, 2025, at 7:00
p.m. for the purpose of a Regular Meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit, City Clerk  Debby Stegura, Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
APRIL 22, 2025
